item.title: Three players, coach earn All-Ohio volleyball honors for 2026
item.description: Three players and a coach from Marion County earned All-Ohio honors from the Ohio High School Volleyball Coaches Association for 2026. For the second year in a row, Pleasant senior Kamryn Cocherl captured first-team honors in Division V. She is a three-time All-Ohioan. Cocherl was 11th in the country and tops in Ohio regardless of division in hitting percentage at .522. She also put down 446 kills, which ranked 19th in Ohio and fifth in Division V, averaging 6.2 kills per set. She served 63 aces and served 92.9 percent to rank third in the Mid-Ohio Athletic Conference. Cocherl added 299 service points, 31 blocks, 196 digs and 225 serve receptions, ranking second on the team in points, digs and serve receptions. Cocherl will play volleyball at NCAA Division I Georgia Southern next season. More on Pleasant volleyball: Pleasant's volleyball legacy lays with the next generation All-MOAC 2026: Top fall athletes named to 2026 All-Mid Ohio Athletic Conference Pleasant teammate Kam Roberts took her first All-Ohio honor, landing on second team as a libero. Her 311 digs were tops in the MOAC and on the team, while adding 267 serve receptions and 88 assists. As a server, she was second on the team and in the league with 58 aces, scoring 287 points on 88.9 serving. She will compete in NCAA Division I at Buffalo. River Valley's Myla Kenney was an honorable mention selection in Division IV as a 6-foot middle hitter/right-side hitter. She led the Vikings in kills with 274, hitting percentage at .336, aces with 47, blocks with 25, digs with 273. Her 247 serve receptions were second-best on the squad. She was an 88.5 percent server and averaged 4.0 kills per set. Pleasant's Kory Ute was given the coaching achievement award in Division V after leading the Spartans to a 26-1 record, winning 78 sets without a loss to start the season. Pleasant won the MOAC title for a second straight season, and it advanced to the Sweet 16 for the fourth straight year, ending as Division V regional runners-up after two straight trips to the Final Four. rmccurdy@usatodayco.com 419-610-0998 X @McMotorsport Instagram @rob_mccurdy_star This article originally appeared on Marion Star: Three players, coach earn All-Ohio volleyball honors for 2026

The FC Bayern II striker only came on as half-time substitute in the game played at DFB-Campus in Frankfurt. The hosts took the lead when Azerbaijani goalkeeper Bilal Hajiyev and midfielder Shikar Shikar created an easy chance for Milo Barde with an unforced error. Before the half-time break, Roko Ciglar doubled Germany's advantage after a well-worked move. Union Berlin's Linus Güther added the third only two minutes after the restart with a brilliant volley. Half-time substitute Assomo scored his four goals in the space of twenty minutes. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Tiger Woods Teases Golf Return & Fans React to His Healthy Look
item.description: Tiger Woods - Tiger Woods (Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Tiger Woods is fueling speculation that his long-awaited return to professional golf is just weeks away, dropping his strongest hints yet about a comeback before the end of the year. The 15-time major champion has not competed in a PGA Tour event since missing the cut at The Open Championship at Royal Troon in 2024. Since then, the 49-year-old golfer has faced several personal and physical challenges, including recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon and his seventh back surgery. His recovery timeline was further delayed earlier this year following a DUI arrest , after which he spent time in a Swiss rehabilitation facility and ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of reckless driving and refusing a breath test in September, resulting in a five-year driving ban. Despite a turbulent year—which also included supporting his partner, Vanessa Trump, through her successful battle with breast cancer—Woods recently ramped up his training, appearing on film hitting balls at Liberty National and Monterey Peninsula Country Club. Tiger Woods says he’s “feeling better” and has been training quite a bit. “I will be at Hero [World Challenge]. I’m there either way, so I’ll see you there!” Could we see Tiger on the course at the Hero in less than a month? https://t.co/4ojh3hW9Rv — SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio (@SiriusXMPGATOUR) November 10, 2026 During a recent interview with SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio, Woods shared an update on his physical status. “I’m feeling better, no doubt about that,” Woods said during his radio appearance. “I’ve been training quite a bit. I will be at Hero [World Challenge]. I’m there either way, so I’ll see you there.” While Woods was previously projected to make his return during the upcoming season opener of the tech-infused TGL league on December 27, his latest comments point toward an earlier appearance. The Hero World Challenge, an exclusive tournament hosted by Woods in the Bahamas, kicks off on December 3. Only three exemption spots remain in the 20-player field, and though Woods is not currently listed among the 17 announced competitors, his comments seem to suggest he intends to tee it up. Related Tiger Woods Breaks Silence After DUI Arrest, Announces Break From Golf Fans on social media were quick to react to his recent remarks, with some pointing out that he appeared healthier. One user commented on X: “Tiger looks ten years younger. Stay on that road — in all senses,” while another wrote: “Whether he tees it up or not, seeing Tiger healthy and upbeat is a win. The man has fought back more than once. Never count him out.” If Woods ends up bypassing the Bahamas event, alternate return options include teaming up with his son, Charlie, at the PNC Championship in Orlando from December 17 to 20, or anchoring Jupiter Links GC when the TGL season begins later that month. item.title: Allofs brothers see their history reflected on El Mala duo
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Cologne's Said El Mala (L) and his brother Malek El Mala are picture after the German Bundesliga soccer match betweem 1.FC Cologne and Bayer Leverkusen at RheinEnergieStadion. (is associated with: «Allofs brothers see their history reflected on El Mala duo») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa Two brothers, one club and a special connection: Klaus and Thomas Allofs see a piece of their own football history reflected in Said and Malek El Mala. Like the El Mala brothers, the Allofs once played together for Cologne. "A pair of brothers like that is something special, it makes the whole story even more emotionally rich," Klaus Allofs told broadcaster Sport1 in an interview. "When the goal was scored, the connection to us was immediately there. I even think that my wife said: 'Look, just like you two back then,'" Klaus Allofs said. He was referring to Said El Mala's goal in the 2-1 defeat to Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday, which was assisted by his brother Malek. His brother Thomas received a photo of the two sets of brothers from friends and acquaintances. "That's when I really realized how extraordinary it is that two brothers play together as strikers in a Bundesliga team," said Klaus Allofs. Forty years ago, the Allofs brothers played together for Cologne. Now, Said and Malek El Mala are making waves in the city. Klaus Allofs is particularly impressed with the younger, Said, who has already made his debut for the Germany national team. "He's an exceptional player," said the former Germany international. "Based on his pure potential, he belongs in the top tier." However, Thomas Allofs sees some challenges for both players. "The pressure on Said and also on Malek is huge. The difficulty is to consistently deliver a good performance," he said. Furthermore, Thomas Allofs believes that constant comparisons between the brothers could also become a burden within a family. Klaus added: "Right now, of course, everything is wonderful. But there will be phases for both of them when things don't go so well."

item.title: Rangers To Probe Seager Trade Market Amid $155M Debt
item.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are ready to listen to offers for shortstop Corey Seager as General Manager meetings start Wednesday in Las Vegas. According to Fox Sports ‘ Ken Rosenthal, the front office expects to hear what other clubs will give up for the star player. The move comes from a team that won the World Series last year.d Series in 2023. Seager carries a massive contract and a no-trade clause, but his value on the field has dropped due to injuries. The Rangers know they must act now before the new Collective Bargaining Agreement changes the rules of the game. The Money Problem Is Real The team’s financial constraints make completing the deal before the season starts difficult. Over the next five years of Seager’s 10-year, $325 million contract, he is owed $155 million. That huge number scares off teams that do not want to take on such a heavy payroll impact. Fox Sports reported that owners are pushing for a salary cap system, which makes other clubs hesitant to absorb that cost. Even with his no-trade clause, the two sides could try to find a fit that works for the player and the club. Health Issues Keep Him on the Sidelines Seager has found it difficult to remain on the field since agreeing to his major contract with the Rangers. He missed time in 2023 with hamstring and thumb issues, then faced sports hernia and hip procedures in 2024. He has not played 150 games in a single season since 2022. His production slipped last year when he played just 102 games and hit only .227. The Rangers need a reliable shortstop, and Seager’s health history includes injuries that could affect his long‑term availability. Yet his elite production when healthy is undeniable and still draws interest from other teams. A Wait-and-See Market Ahead The CBA expires on December 1, and a lockout could stop all deals until owners and players agree on new terms. This uncertainty means the majority of free-agent signings and trades might wait until the new deal is reached. In 12 seasons, he posted a .284 batting average, 241 home runs, 718 RBIs and a 46.3 WAR. The Rangers will explore the market, but a deal depends on finding a team willing to take the risk.

item.title: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured
item.description: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi has been called up to the senior France squad for the first time after Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni both withdrew with injuries. Zinedine Zidane turned to the uncapped striker as a replacement for Thuram, who has been ruled out of France's UEFA Nations League fixtures with a hamstring problem. Thuram picked up the injury on Sunday in Inter's 2-0 Serie A win over Como, a game in which he scored the second goal. Persistent discomfort kept him out of Monday's training session, and he remained under the care of the medical staff. "With no improvement this morning, and following medical examinations, the French national team's medical staff decided, in agreement with Inter and the player, to release him back to his club," France said in a statement on Tuesday . Tchouaméni is also heading home. The Real Madrid midfielder aggravated his right adductor in training, the same injury he suffered at the World Cup in the summer, and will return to Madrid for rehabilitation. Zidane will not call up a replacement for him. Kroupi's route into the squad Kroupi finished as Ligue 2's top scorer in 2025 and was part of the France Under-19 side that reached the final of the 2024 European Championship, finishing as runners-up. The 20-year-old has rejected past advances from Portugal, given his desire to represent France at senior level. He's also eligible to represent Ivory Coast. Kroupi's call-up follows a disrupted start to the campaign. The forward injured his foot during Bournemouth's preseason training camp and needed surgery, only returning to action for the club last month. However, his performances last season have impressed the French set-up. Kroupi scored 13 league goals during his debut Premier League season, a record for a teenager in their first season in the division. Zidane's growing injury list Thuram and Tchouaméni are the latest names on a lengthy list of absentees. Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu has already been ruled out with a left hamstring injury, with uncapped right-back Saël Kumbedi drafted in to replace him. Despite the absences, France lead their Nations League group with 10 points from four games. Zidane's side travel to Italy on Thursday before hosting Türkiye three days later.

item.title: England cancel Windies Test in favour of home Ashes warm-ups
item.description: Sophie Ecclestone has taken five-wicket hauls in her last two Tests [Getty Images] England have cancelled their scheduled Test in the West Indies in April and will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with a number of red-ball matches in the UK. Nat Sciver-Brunt's side have played just one Test - a heavy defeat by India at Lord's - since their last four-day meeting with Australia in January 2025, which they lost by an innings in Melbourne. Next summer's Test against Australia, which is worth four points in the multi-format series, will be held at Headingley from 24-27 June. England will prepare for that with four red-ball matches. One of the games will be a three-day fixture against Australia A before three intra-squad 'best v best' matches. In addition, a dedicated red-ball training camp will be held in Bangalore in January. England expect to use 26 or 27 players across the different training camps and matches. It means England's schedule in the West Indies has been revised to three T20s and three one-day internationals only. The change comes after it was suggested the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) might need to offer financial support to Cricket West Indies (CWI) to allow the Test to take place. "We would welcome any assistance of our much wealthier member boards," CWI chief executive Chris Dehring previously told BBC Sport. "It is very expensive to host cricket in the Caribbean." However, BBC Sport understands the ECB's decision is not related to those financial discussions and the schedule change is viewed as a performance decision in line with giving England the best chance of winning the Ashes. West Indies have not played a women's Test since 2004, which was their only red-ball match in 47 years. "A 10-day warm-weather red-ball camp in India followed by four further matches in English conditions will provide Charlotte Edwards and her team with the appropriate game time to be ready for that challenge [of Australia]," said ECB chief executive Richard Gould. "Best versus best in English conditions provides a valuable opportunity for the team. "It also allows us to assess our strength in depth, give opportunities to more players and get a number of competitive multi-day cricket matches across a longer period into the wider group." item.description: CHICAGO – As Jordan Scott elevated for his sixth and most important block of the night, Dame Sarr turned and watch the ball he shot flying into the expensive seats next to Duke’s bench. Scott came down from the stratosphere of United Center and landed with a guttural yell. Jasiah Jervis gave him a chest-bump, and the rest of his Michigan State teammates hustled over to dap him up, as well. “I might’ve jumped higher than Coen [Carr] over there,” Scott said later with a grin and a laugh. In one swooping moment, and throughout a thorough 79-73 victory over No. 2 Duke in the Champions Classic , the fifth-ranked Spartans delivered a sweeping statement to the Blue Devils and the rest of the college basketball world. "What is that, six blocks to match his jersey number?" item.title: “Kentucky? Who is That?”: Tyran Stokes Talks Smack About Wildcats After Nearly Joining Them as Kansas Wins in Champions Classic
item.description: Tyran Stokes - McDonalds All American Boys Game © Imagn Images The Kentucky Wildcats found themselves on the losing end against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Champions Classic, and, of course, Tyran Stokes played a major role. In his freshman year at Kansas, Stokes delivered a clutch performance, scoring 23 points, 10 rebounds, and four assists against a team he nearly signed with earlier this year as he mulled over his options out of high school. The former five-star recruit had Kentucky as one of his top options before joining Kansas in a major blow to the Wildcats, and he didn’t waste time talking smack about a team he nearly joined. In a now-viral clip from the game, Stokes could be heard talking to his teammates about his 23 points in the game, saying that if this were in March, it could be as much as 40. “Kentucky? Who is that?? And if we see ’em in March?… 40,” he can be heard saying . Tyran Stokes Admitted This Win Felt Personal to Him After the game, Tyran Stokes was understandably over the moon, and he didn’t hold back when asked whether it felt different to put on such a performance against a team he nearly joined this year. “When I chose Kansas and I knew that game was going to be here, it was personal for sure,” Stokes said, per AP News . “But we got the (win) … and that’s all that matters.” Stokes also had Oregon as one of his options before choosing Kansas, but his background from Louisville meant Kentucky remained in the hunt until the very end. “Growing up, obviously you know the tradition and the rivalry between Louisville and Kentucky, so being from Louisville I still got (those) same emotions as if I was playing for Louisville,” Stokes also remarked. item.title: USMNT cancel media access as Man United eye Mauricio Pochettino swoop
item.description: Media duties scheduled for Wednesday have been cancelled by the United States as Manchester United prepare to make a move for their head coach Mauricio Pochettino . It is understood that plans are underway at United to appoint the Argentinian should current head coach Michael Carrick , as expected, be dismissed, with the club currently sitting in the relegation zone after their worst start to a season since 1986. Pochettino is understood to be keen on the Old Trafford post, having previously been linked with the vacancy on prior occasions when it became available. US Soccer confirmed that planned player media access on Wednesday was called off in observance of Veterans Day, removing any opportunity for Pochettino’s squad to be asked about reports regarding his prospective departure. The former Tottenham, Paris St Germain and Chelsea boss signed a contract extension to stay on as USMNT head coach until the 2030 World Cup only three months ago, meaning US Soccer would be owed compensation if he agrees to join United. Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is awaiting clarity on his future (Martin Rickett/PA) (PA Wire) Despite the growing uncertainty surrounding his future, the Englishman arrived for training as normal at United’s Carrington complex on Wednesday morning. He left Carrington on Wednesday afternoon with no announcement on his future having been made. Carrick’s position was discussed by chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in a meeting in Monaco with United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday. A 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como and a 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth had left Carrick’s position under severe threat, but the board chose to grant him the opportunity to turn things around. Carrick’s side subsequently suffered a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, where they failed to take their chances and had Lisandro Martinez sent off, prior to last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win over Roma. An extraordinary 4-4 draw against Aston Villa followed on Sunday, after which the head coach maintained he would not resign and was planning for the international break as usual. "I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there," Carrick said. "Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so. "But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game."
